title: Prick-and-pounce pattern transfer
subtitle: The traditional professional method: pierce holes in the pattern, then rub chalk through to the fabric.
excerpt: Prick-and-pounce is the classic professional embroidery transfer method. Holes are pricked through the pattern, chalk powder is rubbed through the holes onto the cloth, and the dots are then joined with a water-soluble pen before the pattern is lifted.
sourceNotes:
Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776. Prick-and-pounce transfer method.
Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), Internet Archive. Pouncing method for embroidery design transfer.

glossaryTerms.definition: Fine chalk or cuttlefish powder used in prick-and-pounce transfer. Rubbed over the pricked pattern, the powder falls through the holes and marks the fabric below.

content.text: Prick-and-pounce has been used in embroidery workshops for centuries.

passes through pricked holes to leave a dotted copy of the design on the fabric. A water-soluble pen then joins the dots before the pounce blows away. The method produces a clean, accurate transfer and works on any fabric.

items.name: Water-soluble pen (to join dots after pouncing)
Design printed or drawn on cartridge paper

content.text: Place the design right side up on a felt pad or folded cloth (to receive the pricker tip).
Use the pricker to pierce holes at 3 to 4 mm intervals along all the design lines. Hold the pricker vertically and pierce through cleanly.
Run your finger over the back of the pricked paper to smooth down any raised burrs.
Tape the pricked paper to the fabric, right side up. Secure the corners.
Dip the pounce bag in the powder and rub it over the pricked design in small circular movements. Work over every line thoroughly.
Carefully lift the pattern without smearing the powder.
Immediately use the water-soluble pen to join the dots before the powder is disturbed.

items.symptom: The pounce dots blur when the pattern is lifted
items.cause: The pattern was moved before the dots were joined with the pen.
items.fix: Have the pen ready before lifting. Join the dots immediately, before touching or blowing on the surface.

items.symptom: The holes are too far apart and the transferred line is jagged
items.cause: The holes were pricked more than 4 mm apart.
items.fix: Space holes at 2 to 3 mm for curved designs. Straight lines can tolerate 4 mm spacing.

content.text: Prick-and-pounce is the method used for large-scale and detailed professional embroidery.
using this technique allows the same pricked pattern to be used multiple times.
